Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  count(county, sort = T) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   county            n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        25
## 2 Humboldt         20
## 3 San Mateo        19
## 4 Santa Barbara    19
## 5 Marin            16
## 6 Monterey         16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = county, fill = county)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Total Number of Incidents Per County",
       x = "County",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = as_factor(month), fill = month)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Total Number of Incidents By Month",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

sharks %>% 
  count(month, sort = T) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   month     n
##   <dbl> <int>
## 1    10    36
## 2     9    34
## 3     8    31
## 4     7    27
## 5     5    16
## 6    11    16
  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  filter(!is.na(time) & !time %in% c("early am", "afternoon")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time, fill = time)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Total Number of Incidents By Time of Day",
       x = "Time of Day",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

sharks %>% 
  filter(!is.na(time) & !time %in% c("early am", "afternoon")) %>%
  count(time, sort = T) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   time      n
##   <chr> <int>
## 1 11:00    18
## 2 9:00     12
## 3 14:00    10
## 4 17:30    10
## 5 12:00     9
## 6 13:30     9
  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
sharks_injuries <- sharks %>% 
  group_by(county, injury) %>% 
  summarize(total = n()) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = injury, values_from = total)
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'county'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
sharks_injuries
## # A tibble: 22 × 8
## # Groups:   county [22]
##    county                 minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*`
##    <chr>                  <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <int> <int>    <int>
##  1 Del Norte                  2     1    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  2 Humboldt                   2     9     7        1       1    NA       NA
##  3 Island - Catalina          1     3    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  4 Island - Farallones       NA    NA     7       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  5 Island - San Miguel        2    NA     2       NA      NA     1       NA
##  6 Island - San Nicolas       1    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  7 Island - Santa Barbara    NA    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA        1
##  8 Island - Santa Cruz        1     1    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  9 Island - Santa Rosa       NA    NA     1       NA      NA    NA       NA
## 10 Los Angeles                6     2    NA       NA      NA     1        1
## # ℹ 12 more rows
sharks %>% 
  count(county, sort = TRUE) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   county            n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        25
## 2 Humboldt         20
## 3 San Mateo        19
## 4 Santa Barbara    19
## 5 Marin            16
## 6 Monterey         16
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks_injuries %>% 
  mutate(total = sum(across(where(is.numeric)), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(county, total), y = total, fill = county)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Total Number of Incidents by County",
       x = "County",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  count(mode, sort = TRUE) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   mode                    n
##   <chr>               <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding     85
## 2 Freediving             36
## 3 Kayaking / Canoeing    30
## 4 Swimming               22
## 5 Scuba Diving           20
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mode, fill = mode)) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Incidents by Activity",
       x = "Activity",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>% 
  count(species, sort = TRUE) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   species          n
##   <chr>        <int>
## 1 White          181
## 2 Hammerhead       3
## 3 Blue             2
## 4 Killer Whale     2
## 5 Leopard          2
## 6 Salmon           2
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
#Not all incidents involving Great White's are fatal (in fact more are non-fatal)
sharks %>% 
  filter(species == "White") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = injury, fill = injury)) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Number and Types of Incidents for Great White's",
       x = "Injury Type",
       y = "Number of Incidents")
